Project: /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23 (meeting-room booking app; Node 22, built-ins only). Spec: /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/.team/notes/spec.md (read the "Server" section closely). Data layout: /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/.team/notes/backend-api.md. Write ONE new test file: /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/server.startup.test.mjs. Do NOT edit server.mjs, other tests, or the helper. Use the shared helper /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/helpers/server-harness.mjs (read it): `makeTmp(t)`, `spawnServer(dir,{env,cwd})` (env value undefined deletes the var), `startServer(t, dir, {env, cwd})` -> {port, child, out(), err()} (out/err accumulate for the server's lifetime), `boot(t, opts)`, `runToExit(t, dir, {env, cwd})` -> {code, stdout, stderr}, `request`, `post`, `valid`, `assertError`, `portIsFree(port)`. Use node:test + node:assert/strict. Keep the file under ~400 lines (split into server.startup.test.mjs and server.datafile.test.mjs if needed), functions under 50 lines, table-driven loops with a message naming each case, exact equality (never regex/prefix for spec values). No console.log. Tests that spawn many processes can run their spawns with Promise.all for speed. Define a helper `assertOneLine(stderr)`: stderr ends with '\n', contains exactly one '\n', the line is non-empty and does not contain ' at ' (no stack trace). Cases: 1. Invalid PORT -> code 1, stdout '' exactly, assertOneLine(stderr): '+1', ' 80', '80 ', '\t80', '1e3', '0x10', '1.0', '-0', '-1', '65536', '70000', '99999999999999999999', '１２３' (full-width), '٣٠٠٠' (Arabic-Indic), 'abc'. For each, also set DATA_FILE to a file containing 'not json': stderr must NOT equal `cannot read data file \n` (PORT is checked before the data file is read). Run them in parallel. 2. Valid PORT forms: '0' and '00' -> starts, stdout exactly `listening on http://127.0.0.1:

\n` with p > 0 the bound port (verify by a GET /api/rooms on it returning 200). '65535': if portIsFree(65535) start with PORT '65535' and assert stdout is exactly 'listening on http://127.0.0.1:65535\n'; else t.skip. Default port: for env PORT '' and PORT unset (undefined), if portIsFree(3000) start and assert stdout exactly 'listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000\n', then kill the child and wait for its 'exit' before the next case; otherwise t.skip('port 3000 busy'). 3. Port in use (bind a net server on 127.0.0.1:0, use its port) -> code 1, stdout '', assertOneLine. 4. Data file rejected -> code 1, stdout '' exactly, stderr EXACTLY `cannot read data file ${name}\n` where name is DATA_FILE as given. Contents (each its own file): '', ' ', '\n', 'not json', 'null', '[]', '"x"', '1', 'true', '{}', '{"nextId":1}', '{"bookings":[]}', '{"nextId":0,"bookings":[]}', '{"nextId":-1,"bookings":[]}', '{"nextId":1.5,"bookings":[]}', '{"nextId":"2","bookings":[]}', '{"nextId":null,"bookings":[]}', '{"nextId":2,"bookings":{}}', '{"nextId":2,"bookings":null}', '{"nextId":1,"bookings":[],"extra":1}' (extra top-level key), and booking-level problems with nextId 3 and a valid booking B = {"id":1,"room":"Aurora","title":"T","date":"2026-11-03","start":"10:00","end":"11:00"}: duplicate ids (two bookings id 1, different rooms), id equal to nextId (id 3), id greater than nextId, id 0, id '1' (string), id 1.5, extra key in booking ("x":1), missing key (no end), title 5 (number), untrimmed title ' T', empty title '', invalid date '2026-02-30', invalid start '24:00', end before start, room 'aurora', booking that is null, booking that is an array, two overlapping bookings same room/date (ids 1 and 2). Also: a UTF-8 BOM followed by a valid file '{"nextId":1,"bookings":[]}' -> rejected (the server never writes a BOM; stricter reading). Also the path is a directory; the path goes through a regular file (`/data.json`, ENOTDIR) -> rejected. Run in parallel. Name echo: a relative DATA_FILE 'sub/../bad.json' with cwd=dir (bad.json invalid) -> stderr exactly 'cannot read data file sub/../bad.json\n' (folder 'sub' must exist? path.resolve normalises it, so it need not exist — do not create 'sub'); a non-ASCII name 'dätä.json' (invalid content) -> 'cannot read data file dätä.json\n'; DATA_FILE unset and DATA_FILE '' with cwd containing an invalid bookings.json -> 'cannot read data file bookings.json\n'. 5. Valid files load: '{"nextId":1,"bookings":[]}' -> GET {bookings: []}; a file with nextId 7 and two valid non-overlapping bookings ids 2 and 5 (given out of sort order) -> GET returns them sorted; POST gets id 7; the bookings are returned with exact objects. 6. ENOENT: DATA_FILE in a missing nested folder `

/a/b/data.json` -> starts, GET {bookings: []}; a POST gets 500 'internal error' (assertError) and folder `/a` still does not exist afterwards; the server keeps running (GET still 200). 7. Relative paths resolve against cwd, not server.mjs's folder: make `/work/rel/data.json` with a valid booking; spawn with cwd `/work`, DATA_FILE 'rel/data.json' -> GET returns that booking; POST writes into `/work/rel/data.json` (read and parse it, bookings length 2). Default name: cwd `/w2` containing a valid bookings.json with one booking, DATA_FILE unset -> GET returns it; same with DATA_FILE ''. Also check no file named bookings.json was created next to server.mjs (/root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/bookings.json must not exist after these tests if it did not exist before — record existence before). 8. Data file never written except on successful POST/DELETE: write a valid file with one booking; record bytes and mtimeMs (fs.statSync(file).mtimeMs); start server; do GET /api/rooms, GET /api/bookings, GET ?date=2026-11-03, GET ?date=bad (400), POST 415 (text/plain), POST 413 (10001 bytes), POST 400 (bad room), POST 409 (overlap with stored booking), DELETE /api/bookings/99 (404), DELETE /api/bookings/abc (404), PUT /api/rooms (405), GET /nope (404), GET /, GET /app.js; then assert file bytes equal and mtimeMs equal; and the folder holds only data.json (no temp files). Then a successful POST changes the file. 9. Persistence and ids: start with missing file; POST 1, POST 2, DELETE 2 -> file parses with nextId 3; kill SIGKILL, wait for exit, restart with same DATA_FILE -> GET identical to before; POST -> id 3. Then DELETE all bookings, restart, POST -> id 4 (ids never reused even when empty). 10. stdout only ever the one line: start a server whose DATA_FILE is in a missing folder (so POST gives 500 and the server logs something to stderr), do a mixed session (200, 400, 404, 405, 409 is not possible there, 415, 413, 500 POST, DELETE 404), wait ~100 ms, then assert out() exactly equals `listening on http://127.0.0.1:${port}\n`. Run `cd /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23 && node --test test/server.startup.test.mjs` (and the second file if split). If a case fails because the SERVER is wrong per spec, do NOT change server.mjs and do NOT weaken the test: keep it, and report the exact failing case (input, expected, actual). Report: files written, pass/fail counts, suspected server spec violations.

content.content: 1 # Spec (verbatim from the user) — owner: supervisor 2 3 Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Do not use the Fable model. Node v22. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 26 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 27 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. 28 - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). 29 - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. 30 - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. 32 33 Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 34 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 35 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 36 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 37 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 38 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 39 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 40 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 41 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 42 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 43 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. 44 - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. 45 46 Page 47 - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. 48 - The page loads the script with a `

1	# Backend API notes — owner: backend — 2026-11-02
2	
3	Spec: `.team/notes/spec.md` is the source of truth; this note only records implementation choices.
4	
5	## Running
6	- `node server.mjs` (or `npm start`) starts the server. `server.mjs` exports nothing; importing it starts the server.
7	- Tests: `npm test` runs `node --test "test/**/*.test.mjs"`. Plain `node --test test/` does NOT work on Node 22
8	  (a directory argument is treated as a file). Test files must be named `*.test.mjs` under `test/`;
9	  helpers in `test/helpers/` are not run as tests.
10	
11	## Env vars
12	- `PORT`: unset/empty means 3000. Only ASCII digits, value <= 65535, else one stderr line `invalid PORT: <value>`, exit 1.
13	  `PORT=0` means the OS picks the port; the stdout line shows the real port.
14	- `DATA_FILE`: unset/empty means `bookings.json`, resolved against the cwd. ENOENT means start empty (the file is not created).
15	  Any other read error, or content not in the layout below, gives stderr `cannot read data file <DATA_FILE as given>`, exit 1.
16	- Bind failure gives stderr `cannot listen on 127.0.0.1:<port>: <code>`, exit 1.
17	- stdout: only `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>\n`. Unexpected request errors are logged to stderr as one line.
18	
19	## Data file layout
20	`{"nextId": <int >= 1>, "bookings": [{"id","room","title","date","start","end"}, ...]}`
21	Loading is strict: each booking needs exactly those 6 keys, a safe-integer id in 1..nextId-1, unique ids, valid
22	room/date/times, end > start, an already-trimmed title of 1-80 chars, and no two stored bookings may overlap.
23	Anything else counts as "not in this server's layout".
24	
25	## Saving
26	- Written only on a successful POST create or DELETE remove. Writes `<DATA_FILE>.<pid>.<n>.tmp` in the same folder
27	  (flag `wx`), then renames it over the data file; on failure the temp file is removed and the reply is 500 `internal error`.
28	- Memory (bookings and nextId) changes only after the save succeeds. All mutations run one at a time through
29	  an in-process promise queue (overlap check + save inside the queue).
30	
31	## Static files
32	- `GET /` serves `public/index.html` (`text/html; charset=utf-8`), `GET /app.js` serves `public/app.js`
33	  (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`). Paths are resolved relative to `server.mjs` via `import.meta.url`, read per request.
34	  A missing file gives 500 `internal error`; the server keeps running. Other methods on these paths get 405.
35	
36	## Strict readings taken
37	- ENOTDIR (a path component is a file) is not ENOENT, so it gives `cannot read data file`.
38	- HEAD on any known path gets 405 (no auto-HEAD for GET routes).
39	- Overlapping stored bookings in the data file count as an invalid layout.
40

I wrote both test files, but I couldn't run them. The permission system denied my Bash call, so there are no pass/fail counts and no server spec violations to report. Nothing has been checked against `server.mjs`.

I split the cases across two files:
- **`/root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/server.startup.test.mjs`** has cases 1, 2, 3 and 10: invalid and valid `PORT` values, default port 3000, port in use, and stdout holding only the listening line.
- **`/root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/server.datafile.test.mjs`** has cases 4 to 9: rejected data files, the BOM, directory and `<file>/data.json` paths, name echo, valid files, ENOENT, cwd resolution, write discipline and persistence.

To run them: `cd /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23 && node --test test/server.startup.test.mjs test/server.datafile.test.mjs`.

I did not edit `server.mjs`, other tests or the helper.

Things you might not expect:
- **Skips:** the 65535 and default-3000 cases skip themselves if those ports are busy.
